utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Good morning, Mr. Besic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, please continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency. Good morning to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Besic.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, we announced that we would be hearing a viewer calling in live to Radio Hayat, so I would like you to carefully listen. I believe that we don't have a transcript, but -- actually, we did make a transcript, we will have a transcript, so I'm asking you, for us to carefully listen to this viewer. Can we play this 1D1031 from 47 minutes 10 to 47:54. It's some 40 seconds or so.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Go ahead. Salaam alaikum, alaikum salaam. Aganovic on the radio." Interpreter's note, it's very silent, we're not able to hear. "I saw 25 dead, and you know how many people were injured. There is a TV recording of me carrying people. The B and H has already broadcast it. I am speaking the truth. My advice is to organise an extreme party of ours that would kill three Serbs for each one of ours, regardless of whether they're guilty or innocent; guilty for the guilty, innocent for the innocent, because our people are not [as interpreted] innocent."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you able to hear, Mr. Besic?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was able to hear the words of this man. These are the words of one individual who is bitter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, let's leave aside this recommendation of his to kill three for one, and let us focus on what he says; that he was an eye-witness, that he helped in the evacuation, and that he saw 25 bodies. Now I would like to ask you, Mr. Besic, whether you believed, without doubt, your associates or people who spent an hour there, without notifying the police, and did you believe everything that they said?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President. I think the question assumes matters which are not yet in evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: "Because our people are innocent."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What is your objection again, Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: In the question, he states that. "... your associates or people who spent an hour there, without notifying the police ..." I don't believe that there is evidence on the record to that effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That part, yes. Could you reformulate your question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought that the document that we saw yesterday has already been admitted. I would like to tender it now, the document, in which it says that the explosion occurred at 1220 hours and that the notification arrived at 1320.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Without making a submission, I told you to reformulate your question to the witness this time, based upon this radio broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, this eye-witness who helped in the evacuation of those who were killed, and who says that he can be seen on the footage of TV Sarajevo that broadcast this, he said that he saw 25 bodies. They told you, after you arrived -- without you having seen a single body, they told you that there was 68 bodies. My question refers to the following. I'm not going to imply that you participated in that, but you were told, so my question is: Did you believe what you were told or do you have any basis for any doubt when you compare these two pieces of data?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Incoming information came from several sources. It was not our job to count and to take this information for what it was worth. We came to process the cream of the sign [as interpreted]. The number of dead was registered in the Kosevo morgue. That number is 68 bodies. And then later, some other people died. They succumbed to their injuries. According to this person -- this was a person who was not able to speak directly to the police. This is something that he stated for Hayat Radio, so we should not really take into account his figure of 25 bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. But my question will also refer to the following. Did you also believe them, as far as the scene of the crime was, in other aspect as well? But we will come to that. My question -- actually, my position is that they were hiding something from you and that you did not get complete information. This is one of the elements, and soon we will see other elements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Karadzic. Who are you referring to by "they"? I have difficulty following your line of questions, but you said that the gentleman in the broadcast said he saw 25 bodies, and then they told the witness there were 68 bodies. Do you mean that he hid something or he counted all the bodies and he came to the number of 25? I don't follow your lines of questions. Could you clarify?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. Since the witness and I are from the same area, certain things are implied between us. This is what I want to clarify: There is an hour from the explosion to the time that the police were notified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So that's the subject of your further submission, but put your question, if necessary, to the witness. Or, if necessary, I will ask the witness to be withdrawn from the courtroom and I'll give you an opportunity to address the Chamber as to your defence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps after the break. Can we now have -- can we now have 65 ter 09620.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you like to tender that broadcast?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The two documents that we saw yesterday, I would like to tender those, and this recording that we heard a little bit earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like to object to the admission of the recording. First of all, there's nothing in the audio section that we heard which suggests that this was actually a broadcast from Radio Hayat. What we do have is an audio-recording accompanied by a screen shot, and there's -- it's something of a mystery to us why the audio-recording from a radio broadcast is accompanied by a screen shot purporting to show a Radio Hayat. There's been no evidence led that this is a genuine broadcast of Radio Hayat. We dispute the authenticity of this recording.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And the witness was not able to confirm whether or not it was a Radio Hayat broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think all the documents dealt with yesterday were admitted at the time. What documents do you refer to?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 09634 and 09622. I thought that they were tendered, but I misunderstood the intervention by Mr. Gaynor, that I was asking something that has not been admitted into evidence yet. So these are the two reports and the -- actually, a report and the record which we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did we see 9622 yesterday?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have any observation, Mr. Gaynor? 9634 and 9622.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I have no observations regarding those two. My objection is limited to the broadcast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Okay. They will be admitted and will be given a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. 65 ter 9634 will be Exhibit D892, and 65 ter 9622 will be Exhibit D893. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. Let me just say this much: We submitted a very long recording, but we cannot play the whole thing. This is a call-in show with callers telephoning in. We have that. This is something that can be checked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark this recording for identification, until the time when we'll be satisfied as to its authenticity and foundation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D894, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at 65 ter 09620, please. This is photographic evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise this first page?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, your signature is at the bottom; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at page 6, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Since we're not quite sure where this arrow is, would you be able to mark on this photograph the place of the explosion? The text speaks of an arrow here, but we are not able to see it.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, because this documentation was compiled very quickly, we actually did not put the arrow in. It should be here [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please date and initial this photograph?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we tender this photograph, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D895, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You stated that you saw the fins and that you did not touch anything until the UNPROFOR arrived. Would you like me to call up that part of your statement?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That is correct, I looked at the scene of the crime, the inner and the broader area. I did see the stabiliser. I looked in the centre and I found the stabiliser embedded below the surface. And taught from my experience the day before, when I was working at Dobrinja, when seven people were killed, when the stabiliser also embedded itself into the surface, so taught by experience, when I didn't find a stabiliser aboveground, I found it embedded deep in the ground. Since there were rumours about sabotage and so on, I thought it better that the UNPROFOR should carry out this investigation because they were more likely to be believed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. So you looked around and you didn't see the fins outside, you saw them inside, and you waited for some 10 or 15 minutes for the UNPROFOR to arrive, and then they arrived and that was that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we waited for some 10 or 15 minutes, they arrived pretty quickly, and then we began.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at P17013 -- actually 09, page 13. P1709, that is a Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting, Mr. Besic, my question is: Did you believe that during that hour, nobody touched that point of impact?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we are having some problems here because of this time. The explosion, itself, and the fatalities occurred at 12.20. We received the information in some 10 to 15 minutes, and the investigation began at 1320. We took about 40 minutes to get there, and that's when the investigation began. However, the person who conducted the investigation report, it wasn't myself, it was someone else. It's up to me to process the scene of the crime, while the operatives would compile all the data, all the information about the investigation, and then we have some. But if you think that you can do something in 40 minutes, that you can stage something, how much time do people need throw the corpses around? You cannot do that in 20, 30, 40 minutes. Some time is required for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The document from yesterday indicates that there was an hour between the explosion and the notification of your service. On the other hand, do you agree that those who were loading the corpses did not have to do anything at the point of impact? After that, some other team could have been working simultaneously at that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't agree with that. When the explosion occurred, when the people were wounded and taken away, the police from Stari Grad were automatically engaged to secure the scene of the crime. No one could enter the scene until the investigation team arrived. I am sure of that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, we will see. Can we have page 13 of this document now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what this scale at the side stands for?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We use this scale to determine the size, the length of the object. Specifically, in this case, this is a mortar shell -- a stabiliser from a mortar shell. The fields are divided here, black-and-white fields, and they are of 1-centimetre size. So then we have an overview of the size of the object. When you count the fields, then you could conclude that this stabiliser is 20 centimetres' long.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So each of the fields, the black and the white fields, are 1 centimetre in size; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now look at P1967. This is the stabiliser that we have here in the courtroom. Can we have the previous exhibit back, please, the previous photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can I ask you, Mr. Besic, to measure? We have a ruler here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, let us up-load the previous exhibit, Exhibit P1709, in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How long is the stabiliser, Mr. Besic?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 16 and a half or 17 centimetres. There is a difference of 3 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, you did not measure from 0. I think the difference is more. But 3 centimetres is a significant difference, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that in this case -- no, I don't see any reason -- whether it's 20 or 19, the stabiliser is damaged. When you compare the photographs with this, I think it's identical, regardless of the 3 centimetres' difference, 4, 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you look at this groove on the left surface of the stabiliser. Can you find that groove that goes through these three holes? Can you find that on that stabiliser? On the left, you see the groove, a rip?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's here [indicates]. If you look at these three here and you see those three there, here it is, it's here [indicates]. You would have to look at it under a light at an angle. The blitz was actually used -- the flash was used in this direction, so this is how it is.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The speakers are kindly asked not to overlap.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you compare these three holes, one, two, three, and if you compare these three with the photographs, you will see the three grooves which are photographed under the flash. And if you look at that under an oblique light, you will be able to see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If that's an important part, we have difficulty following these lines of questions without having the possibility to really look at what part -- to which part the witness is indicating. If necessary, I'm wondering whether we can put it on the ELMO and we can follow which part is indicated. Put a paper on the ELMO to protect the screen. So could you measure it again?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Besic, bear in mind it doesn't start from the beginning. There is a certain numbering.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The length is 17 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll have to measure it for ourselves. I think it's considerably less. But even that is less than what is shown on the picture, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's a problem with this photograph. The problem is this: If you look at the ends here, if you look at the ends -- the edges here on the photo, you will see that the object was laid down like this [indicates] to be photographed. To straighten it, you have it straightened up like this [indicates], and the length appears longer. It's no longer 17, but it's 22. This is the position as it was photographed [indicates]. Do we see this clearly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could Mr. Besic push his hand a little further up the screen? It's not visible on the television. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. This image is what we see in the picture.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If somebody could give me a pen or a pencil. Do we agree that these three openings are seen on the photograph here on the right? Do we agree about that, these three holes? And when you compare this semicircle here [indicates] -- can you see it? There it is on the photo. Below it, there are three openings, three holes, one, two, three. If you twist it just a little bit, you get these openings [indicates]. It's a bit hard to explain this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm telling to the Audio-Video, is it not possible to show what is seen on the ELMO for the purpose of the record?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Could you explain again, if you could, in a nutshell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a bit of a problem, but I'll try. If we look at the photograph on the screen, on the right we see damage to this part here [indicates]. Right? Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just go on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We see this damage here.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just go on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Above this damage, you see three holes, and you can see them on the photo, on the right, also. I would prefer it if you could see it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I am switching between two screens and I can see clearly what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can see it clearly, those three holes, but on the ELMO it's difficult to see. We have to keep turning the object around, and that's why it's a bit uncomfortable, it's a bit awkward.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could I ask you to measure from the bottom to the edge? There's a ruler there. It shows the entire length. It's 22 and a half centimetres; right?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I've just explained, to be photographed, this object was not straight up at a 90-degree angle, because it drops, and that's why we got this other length. Look at the difference. It's certainly a 3-centimetre difference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you move your hand a bit further up? To the opposite direction; yes. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see, it's not able to stand up on its own, so our colleague who did this, Suad Dzumisic, had to photograph it in this position [indicates], and this is how, what the photograph shows. This is the position you see on the photograph, and in this position it has that length.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the proper position [indicates], and look that this is not vertical, it's not at a 90-degree angle. This is what we call a macro-photograph. It should have been photographed this way [indicates]. However, it was photographed like this [indicates], if not even further up. Right, this is how the photo was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So it was not really done properly, was it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, under the circumstances in which we worked, I think the work was done great, it was fabulous. With those shortages of proper conditions and material, the work was great.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If we look from this perspective, if we raise the object, it becomes longer, not shorter; right? Try to raise it. Do you see that it becomes shorter? Visually, it looks shorter if you raise it, if you prop it up. If you drop it, it will be longer. You'll see.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can't be longer. Anyway, the difference is 2, 3 centimetres, not more, if that makes a whole bit of difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We have lined paper, if you want to take it. It shows exactly how much you lose in length if you prop it up.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if these lines are with an interval of 1 centimetre.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: They're not, but it doesn't matter. Just drop it. It's shorter, you see. Now raise it. You'll see that it gains in length, at least visually.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But you have to look at the edge. The edge begins here [indicates], not there [indicates]. I know you'd like it to start from there, but it starts, actually, from the bottom edge. That's where we gain in length, those 2, 3 centimetres. That's how you measure it, from the bottom edge.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now call up another photograph, the photograph of the scene. No, first we'll watch a video, 40125, starting with H-43 to H-47. It's been admitted. Let's just view it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it the way it appeared the first glance you got?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this was set up after the scene was cleared. It was set up by Mirza Sabljica and the other man. I can't recall his name, the one who died.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I hope it's not Mirza Sabljica who died.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Zlatko Medjedovic, you mean?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You say something was cleared here?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cleared this area here, I personally cleared it. And after I removed blood and tissue and all sorts of objects, Mirza Sabljica and his colleague came, set this -- laid these staffs to try to determine the direction. So it's not I who laid these sticks. That's not the first photograph. The first photograph showed the scene before clearing. You can see the debris, the blood, the body parts, everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On this photo, you can't see the fins. The fins are 7 to 9 centimetres below ground?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. I've already -- I had already told my colleagues that the stabiliser is inside, but nobody wanted to touch it. We were waiting for UN members to arrive. We wanted to avoid any possibility of further manipulation or speculation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All this has been admitted, so let me play it again. We don't have to worry about minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the scene as you found it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. You see for yourself. The picture speaks for itself. You see that nothing has been cleared.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your practice, did you encounter cases where the stabiliser was embedded so deep into the tarmac that it was 7 to 9 centimetres below ground?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. It happened just the day before this in Dobrinja. It's in the documentation. The stabiliser was stuck into the ground 3 to 4 centimetres' deep.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This one is not even visible. To reach it, you have to dig 7 to 9 centimetres?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You don't need to dig. If you take the surface of the asphalt and the material thrown on top, it's just a few centimetres. It's visible above the asphalt.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So the one in Dobrinja was visible?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And it protruded from the ground?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you encounter any cases where the whole stabiliser went deep into the ground?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, the colleagues I worked with and I encountered such cases. Sometimes it fell so deep inside, we were not able to find it at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Into the tarmac?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sometimes they would be stuck into the asphalt.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you explain to all of us, this is an explosion, not an implosion?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I'm not a ballistics expert, but as a layman, I don't see the difficulty. A mortar shell travels at an angle and falls at an angle. The fuse does its job, the body explodes, and the stabiliser continues on the trajectory and embeds itself into the ground, which is already softened by the explosion. The hard obstacle is already removed, so the stabiliser gets stuck into the surface.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Since it's not an implosion, but an explosion, how come that so much fine debris found its way into the hole?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you that. Probably due to the detonation. As the explosion occurred and the stabiliser got stuck into the ground, the fine debris covered this hole again. I don't believe, honestly, that somebody took a handful of earth and threw it inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you take a look at the screen and tell us whether this is the stabiliser of the shell in Dobrinja which landed in soft soil?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. It's not soft soil, actually. It's tarmac. You can see it clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But there is no debris that covered the hole again?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. It all depends on the angle of descent. I really can't comment on this in any expert way. I'm not a ballistics man, but I can see things as a layman. It's quite obvious, in three or four examples, including Markale I and Markale II, that the stabiliser got stuck into the tarmac, and it's possible that it stuck 7 or 8 or 5 centimetres' deep.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here is my theory, Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: For the record, what is the exhibit number for this?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's 1D2867. Time, 7.49 to 8.01.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Which hasn't yet been admitted, Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No, this video has not been admitted. There's no objection to the admission of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you like to tender that part?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, this part of the film.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This part will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D896, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But I would like to remind you of your responsibility to up-load this part. Yes, let's carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's the Defence case, Mr. Besic, that the debris on the scene of Markale I was brought in artificially and used to artificially cover this scene after the impact, and that's what took one hour before your arrival.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot comment on that. I know that these are the facts, both with regard to the crime scene investigation in Dobrinja and in Markale I, and I stand by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then we have to lead evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call up in e-court 65 ter 40125. It's a video and a still from that video. It would be from 7:11 to 7:15. 1D851 is the still from that video -- D2851.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On this photograph, would you please circle the point of impact, if you can? Is this the point of impact?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. Yes, this is the place of impact. You see damage on the tarmac. This is the center. All this is damage [marks], and further afield.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, use the red pen to mark this little plate in the left bottom corner with the hole in it, a platelet.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean where the date is [marks]?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's the date, but the platelet is in the corner.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here in the corner [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark it with "1"?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is taken before you did anything?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the situation as we found it. Our work is to record the situation as found, and then to clear, and then to collect evidence and document it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you initial and put a date?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D897, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now see 65 ter 40125 from 6:46 to 7:12.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the area around the point of impact that has been cleared?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now get the still, 1D02853. It's a still from this video.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is the place before clearing -- sorry, after clearing, but before digging out the tail-fin?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where is that platelet from the previous picture?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really have no idea. I can't see it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we tender this part of the film and this still -- or, rather, just the still?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D898, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we again see that same footage from 9:15 to 9:18.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now get a still, 1D2855. 1D2855.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On this picture, can you see that platelet?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it. It's from the door lock.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you put a circle and number 1 around it? The tail-fin has been dug out and we can see the fins. It's a still from the video we've just seen.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. [Marks]. Which number?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Number 1, your signature and date.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it clear to you now that this platelet is glaring proof that this scene has been tampered with? First, the place was cleared, then it was gone, and then after the tail-fin was dug out, it appeared again.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree. It's a mobile piece of debris that anyone could have kicked away. That it had been there before the explosion, it's out of the question. It was very near the surface. Anyone could have shifted it from -- with their foot. It could have landed here. It's just a decorative piece on the door frame. It's much better visible on the photograph than in the film. It's a yellow brass colour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have this photograph admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D899, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see again 1D02853. Can we have both photos at the same time on a split screen. Keep this photo and put 1D02853.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, look carefully. Near this metal thing, what can we see? We see the cleared scene. Where is the platelet at this moment?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this moment, I don't see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before you -- already you answered. Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I just wanted to point out for the Court that there are much higher -- crisper -- higher-definition, crisper versions of these photographs in P1970, photographs number 4 and 7. I simply want to make the Court aware of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, and the degree of zooming in is also different. Yes, can you take a look at P1970. You mean on the right side?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, the photograph on the right side should be P1970, page 7, and the one on the left should be P1970, number 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I beg your pardon, but I take it that this --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, the degree of zoom is entirely different in the two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, no, but I'm not sure whether this picture is identical to 1D2853. 1D2853 is taken from the -- is a still from the video, but this pictures is a --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Photographs --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- photograph taken by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We have to confirm, then, this photograph is identical to the scene from the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. We can do that now or I can do it in redirect, as Your Honours wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So can you compare the two photos, the one on the left side, still - we'd like to see the still, which is 1D2853 - and this picture, the right-side picture? We have to be satisfied the two photos -- two images are identical. If the Defence accepts this or -- Mr. Besic, can you help us with this, whether the two images are showing the same place at the same time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It's just that they are photographed from different angles. This one is from 90 degrees and the other one is from a slightly greater distance and at an angle. But when you take the markings on the asphalt surface, then you can tell that it's identical.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Besic, before any cleaning, we see the tile?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But this has been cleared.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, I'm speaking about the first photograph that I showed to you when you arrived, before you did anything. We see the tile. Then we don't see the tile. Then it's dug out and we see the tile?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am saying again, and I stand by that, there is a possibility -- you are seeing on these photographs footprints of people who are moving around, people from the investigation team. It's possible that somebody took the tile, accidentally kicked it. It just happened to be there by accident. It has nothing to do with anything. It's just a tile. It's on the photograph, on the video footage. On the photograph, we see it there after the surface around the center around the centre of the explosion was cleaned. The tile is there. The tile is also there at the moment when the centre was being cleaned. It's there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. That remains to be analysed further by us. Can we now have the footage from 0:13 to 0:19, and then we'll take a still from there. From 0:13 to 0:19.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The photograph is 1D2856.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the place of the explosion, Mr. Besic?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What can we see on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the street that divides the market from this building in 22nd December Street, Dvanaestog Decembra. We know which building that is. And then there are stands along the building. It's a small street. It's 3 metres' wide. That exit onto Mustafa Baseskije Street, the explosion landed from the right side, and this is damage that was created.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And in relation to this red piece of furniture, this trunk, where is the place of explosion?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You don't see it from here. It's some 7 to 8 metres away from there to the right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at 1D2856. This is a film still, but can we look at 1D2856, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In relation to this box, the explosion is to the right; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, some 7 to 8 metres.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, we will leave that. We don't need to tender this. Can we now have 1D1031, please. 1D1031, this is the film footage from 1:04:20 to 04:22.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see -- do you recognise Markale I here, Mr. Besic?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, I recognise it very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have the photograph from the film, 1D2857.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When was this recorded, Mr. Besic?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. I don't know. I think that -- I really -- I don't know. I can't tell. I think that this was not recorded by the CSB staff, specifically by my colleague Mr. Sadikovic. I don't think that he recorded that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So there were a number of people who were filming. You said that there weren't.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm only speaking about the CSB staff. Sadikovic, he did not film this. As for others, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we play this footage so that you can see what this looks like and for us to -- and for you to tell us what one can see here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before that, could you give the 65 ter number of this again?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D1031. This is a 1D Defence exhibit, 1D1031.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is -- well, can you please pay attention, if you recognise anyone. Who is this gentleman? Do you know this man?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know him personally, but I assume that on the basis of his accreditation or ID, that he could have been a member of the Stari Grad police force. I don't know him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that at this point in time, there are no items for sale on the stalls anywhere?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But you can see from the previous recording that people were gathering their things on the stalls. Some people were also collecting tissue, extremities and so on. So this footage started from some person who was put into a vehicle. The leg remained behind. Later, it was put inside. I don't know whether this is a police force member. I thought that I could tell by the ID, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Besic, are you able to tell me how come that the artificial leg from the sidewalk is being taken back to the market, and why?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know why they did that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. I'm confused with the number. What is the number for this video?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The entire footage is 1D1031.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: 1D1031 was the number for the Radio Hayat broadcast.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a part of an exhibit of the Defence, an audio-visual compilation of what was broadcast on Bosnian television and radio, Your Excellency. And for the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. So it is your explanation that the audio file and video file were all compiled in one compilation by the Defence; is that your explanation?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This was broadcast on Muslim television. We see the artificial leg here that was left at this place.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The words which appeared in red a moment ago were, I believe, placed there by the Karadzic Defence. I want to note that for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I still have difficulty allocating the number. 1D1031 was allocated as the radio broadcast, and what we marked for identification was only those parts . So I would recommend you to use another 65 ter number for the future purpose.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is fine. Can we then have this treated as 1D1031.2?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: 1031A, following the practice of the Prosecution. But let's carry on. 1D1031A refers to the video shots of the Markale I after the incident. So where are we, Mr. Karadzic? What is your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you this now, Mr. Besic: In your opinion, can a shell land at a place like this without hitting any of the stall roofing, can it fall between the buildings? You know what this opening looks like that faces the north/north-east as is the incoming direction believed to be. How come that the shell didn't affect anything else?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you're mistaken. You saw that the roofing of the stalls were used as stretchers for people to take corpses away to the morgue, but this roofing was ripped off before. There was a lot of destruction. A lot of the stalls were moved, turned to the side as people were being taken out. And you can see this cart that was used for transporting the corpses, and even you can see, next to the cart, a corpse. People were using all kinds of things that were there in order to help the casualties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sorry for my frequent intervention. But, Mr. Karadzic, what we seeing on the e-court monitor is 1D2857? It's a --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The photographs -- the stills from the film we treated differently. We gave them a different number. The number of the footage is the one that we gave. This is a still taken from the footage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. For the record, Mr. Besic, could you read the B/C/S part which appears on that screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says: "Artificial leg after the explosion."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, I understand that an explosion ripped some roofs away. But on contact with a stall roofing, would the shell have been activated?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since it's a plastic part, I'm sure that it would have, I think that it would have, but it didn't touch any roofing. It just landed like that. It could have touched the supermarket roof, but it didn't land there. It landed where it landed, and what happened, happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. It kind of slipped through to quite a degree, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I assume that you know what a mortar shell is like. A person with a good eye and good firing elements can fire wherever they want.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is the distance between the roofs? What is the distance between the roofs of the stalls?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if it's a metre, or maybe not even that. The place where it exploded, there is a line of stalls along the supermarket. Then there's a space of some metre wide, and then along the length the stalls are arranged. There is a metre or a metre 20 width there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we agree, Mr. Besic, that if we imagine a circle -- a concentric circle around the explosion, that 40 per cent of the circle would then go to the wall of the neighbouring building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have to clarify that for me, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The shell landed close to a wall; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That wall actually is just like a supporting wall that is a metre broad, and then you have the proper wall of the supermarket. And the stalls are arranged along this front short wall, and then there is a line of stalls there, and then there is a line of the other stalls.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What I'm trying to say: In that part, 35 to 40 per cent of the circle, in that area there were no people because that is the space that is occupied by the wall; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You cannot get to the wall because the stalls are there. The stalls are leaning against this short wall. It's some 30 to 40 centimetres' width between the proper wall and this shorter wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, I state that a large number of the shrapnel did not dissipate in this area of the circle that is some 60 per cent of its overall area. They all went into the area of the 40 per cent of the circle, where the wall -- how do you explain that? The wall is there which cuts at a tangent this area where the shrapnel dissipated, so can you imagine that there was an equal number of people on all four sides? In that case, how can you explain that there are so many people who were killed and wounded in that area?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before you answer, Mr. Besic: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: It appeared to me, Mr. President, that we're heading into the area of expert evidence concerning the distribution of shrapnel following an explosion. This isn't the correct witness for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, this witness is not and does not ever claim to be an expert in ballistics or the way in which shrapnel is likely to be distributed by an explosion. His expertise is ex post facto. In addition, you are actually giving evidence as much as you're asking questions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I apologise. We can withdraw that. I just wanted to point to the fact that it was not a full circle. I wanted to confirm from the witness that there was no full circle of distribution or dissipation, because it dropped close to the wall. All right, we'll do that with another witness. All right. Can we now move to Markale II.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is an incident which you also investigated; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was your task in the incident?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just like the previous incident of Markale I, in Markale II my task was the same, which means that I had to look at the scene of the crime, make the video footage, make a sketch, and collect material evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When did you arrive at this scene of the incident?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably we will have some problems again between the time of notification and arrival. You need to be flexible, if I may put it that way. It is chaos, after all. Times were different. So this was an identical situation. We need from 40 to an hour's time in order to set up the investigation team, so it took us, again, 40 to 50 minutes to form a team which then came to the scene. Some came by car, some walked. In any case, we all met up in front of Markale, and the investigation began pursuant to the instructions by the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Before you began the investigation, there was some actions that were done there before. How did you find the place when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You need to clarify "actions." "Actions," what do you mean? Are you talking about the buildings or did something happen when we arrived there? The investigation came. When we came, we found a clear area without anyone at the location. It was secured by the Centar Police Administration personnel so that nobody was actually at the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Again, in your team, did you have your own videographer?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. This was Suad Dzumisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And did the police have any other videographers for these incidents?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, always one would be part of the team. He is part of the team, only one; no one else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was the street closed to traffic before the explosion and at the time of the explosion?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the street was open. Vehicles were able to move. The trams were not operating, so whoever had petrol could drive. After the explosion, after the incident, no vehicles passed. It was not possible because the area was secured.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But a vehicle did pass and damaged the stabiliser; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. The stabiliser -- you saw the footage, you saw the chaos, and you saw how many vehicles passed. Nobody was taking -- paying attention to the stabiliser, the stabiliser was probably damaged by one of the vehicles. It was flattened. It wasn't even found at the place where it was supposed to be. It was someone 2 to 3 metres away from the explosion. But it's a movable piece of evidence that somebody can accidentally kick away. So you cannot always determine its fixed place, as was the case in Markale I with the stabiliser.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you get information that a vehicle was damaged that was passing by at the moment of the explosion? Did you have information that any vehicles were there in the street at the point of explosion?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know of any such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And who was securing the scene?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The scene was secured by the police of the Centar SUP or MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I need to make pauses. I believe that the interpreters are having difficulties with the two of us. So can we say when -- can you say when the investigation began?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure whether we started in 40 minutes or in an hour, but it was certainly within the hour that the investigation began. The time was from 40 minutes to 1 hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. At that point in time, did you find the UNPROFOR there or did UNPROFOR representatives arrive later, after you came to the scene and began your investigation?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my photo documentation, you can see photographs on the first or second page. You can see what the scene looked like from two directions, and you can see that there is nobody -- there isn't a single person in that area, which means that the scene was secured and no one was there until we arrived. The first person who entered that scene was myself. This is the case for Markale I and Markale II, because it's my job to photograph the scene as I found it, and to photograph the center of the explosion, and to collect evidence. I was also, throughout that whole activity, recorded by my colleague, Mr. Suad Dzumisic. If you look at the footage, you'll be able to see me cleaning the center of the explosion. This time I used a broom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Before you arrived, the chaos, the evacuation, all of that preceded the cleaning that you did and the whole investigation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason why we came was what happened, what we saw on the recording. After the victims were helped and the bodies were taken away, the police automatically secured the scene of the incident. A team was formed. In order for the team to have been formed, the Communications Centre had to have been notified. An order was issued for the team to form, and the team then went to the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you make the sketch which is part of the documentation?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not make a sketch, but I did help my colleague, Salko Cerimagic. The two of us did it together, after everything was cleared up and everybody went off.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have 65 ter 09899, please. 09899. And then after identifying the first page, can we please look at page 3. I hope that, Your Excellencies, you will tell me when the break is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If it is convenient, we will take a break now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: When we resume, I ask you, Mr. Karadzic and Mr. Besic, to put a pause between your questions and answers. We'll have a break for half an hour. We will resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, we will discuss other incidents while my associates review the material we have recently received. We got this video, for instance, just before we came into the courtroom, and we haven't had time to view it fully. But we are thankful to you for bringing it. May I now ask you if you participated in the investigation of the incident of the 24th, the day before Markale?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was your role there?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just as in the case of Markale, it was the same with Dobrinja I or Dobrinja II; investigating the crime scene and all the actions involved. Let me not repeat.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then I need not call up this record of on-site investigation, on which your name features. We can call up 09167, but I believe it's been admitted already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Just for the record, I think there may have been an interpretation error. I believe that the question might have related to the Dobrinja incident on the 4th of February, which was one day before the Markale I incident, which was on the 5th of February.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought I said the same, but I did not mention Dobrinja, just the date, the 4th of February. Could we now look up 1D2191, a plan of Dobrinja. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark on this map the place where the incident occurred, the one you investigated? Do you agree that this street is marked as "353," "Sarajevo Liberator Street," "Ulica Oslobodilaca Sarajeva"?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The street is called the Bulevar of Sarajevo Defenders, 352.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that it's 353? It crosses the Bulevar of Mimar Sinana?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is it, and this is the plateau where the shell landed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that these lines, the vertical lines, point north-south?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat that question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that these vertical lines, like on any map, show the directions north-south?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Parallel with this vertical line, would you draw a line that goes north-south across this street of Sarajevo Defenders?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you put the letter N for "North" at the top, the date, and your signature?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D900, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You are one of the authors of the photo documentation in the investigation of this incident; correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us why this photo documentation does not include the place where the projectile landed in this street outside number 8? And to assist you, I'll call up 65 ter 09617. Can we see the Serbian. The Serbian version -- the cover page of the Serbian version is ERN 1025-804, 804. The 65 ter is 09617, and ERN is 1025-804. Is this the cover page of the photo file for this incident?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now see page 22.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the place?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the plateau behind the garage in the said street. It's the broader view of the place where two projectiles landed. We see one arrow, and the other arrow is to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did two or three shells land?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to eye-witnesses, there were three. We processed only two of them because they inflicted a lot of damage and five or six people were wounded. The third shell did not inflict much damage and did not hurt anyone, so we did not work on it. It was all done in agreement with the prosecutor, I think, Zdenko Eterovic, or, rather, he was the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree it would have been easier to determine all the elements based on three points of impact instead of two?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. But even with one or two points of impact, you can determine the direction from which the projectile came.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you mark on this photograph where this third shell landed in red?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You don't see that area on this photograph. It fell behind, on the Ulica Branilaca Sarajeva Street, behind these buildings, not in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then we won't deal with that incident anymore, because you did there the same as in every other incident. You collected the evidence and made the photo documentation?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But I'd like to know why the photo documentation doesn't include that third point of impact, regardless of whether you worked on it or not?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we couldn't include it because we did not work on it. We did not investigate that impact. We concentrated on the first two.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to focus on the incident of 18 November 1994. That's Attachment 4 on Schedule F. It's an incident involving Dzenana Sokolovic and her son. Did you investigate that incident?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The leader was Ermin Kazic. I was assisting him in case he needed assistance, but I did go to the scene and I know what that incident involved.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see 65 ter 10418.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In the meantime, can I just make a brief observation, Mr. Karadzic. You asked the witness to mark on the map, and we admitted as evidence as D900, which we saw already several times before. But you didn't ask any question in relation to this, so I find it sort of wasting time. So take into account such factors in the future.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe we did not waste more than one minute, Your Excellency, but it was important for us that the witness confirm the place and the orientation according to the azimuth. I hope it was not too wasteful. Can we see page 2 of this document. I did get a satisfactory answer regarding the place of the incident, and the fact that the third shell was not dealt with, and concerning the orientation to the north. Page 2, please. Next page, the official report. Next one, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Under number 5, do you see your name in a list of seven members of the investigating team?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was this document signed by the same person, Salko Alimagic [as interpreted], who was on the scene with you 28th of August? Cerimagic, Salko Cerimagic. How is Mr. Salko Cerimagic signed here?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As an inspector, I believe, because it is inspectors who make official reports from the crime scene, listing everyone who came out to the scene, and they describe the incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This incident took place in November 1994. How come that in August 1995, he was signed as a scene-of-crime officer?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Salko normally was a scene-of-crime officer, even before the war. But during the war he was transferred from one service to another by virtue of his superiors' orders, and from scene-of-crime officer he became an inspector in the CSB.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That would have been a promotion. However, this is not a promotion. In 1994, he was an inspector. In 1995, he was a scenes-of-crime officer.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then I -- then I confused the two. But his title is "scenes-of-crime officer." That's his position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know exactly where this incident took place?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's on the crossing of these streets, Franjo Racki Street and Zmaja od Bosne Street.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see 1D2858.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting, where was the injured party, Dzenana Sokolovic, at the time that the shell hit, on the pavement or on the driveway?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the driveway, because most of that street was protected by rubbish containers stacked one on top of another.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise, on this aerial photograph, these buildings?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me try to find my way here. I don't see any landmarks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see, in the park, the buildings of the land museum, then the Franjo Racki Street which crosses what was formerly Zmaja od Bosne Street, then the university buildings, then the government buildings? Can you use those as landmarks to mark the place of the incident? You can see the municipality building and the Executive Council.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you can help me, is this the Vrbanja Bridge [marks]?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that case, the incident was here [marks]. I see the Catholic Church. Looking from this side, it's 50 to 100 metres away from the church. Dumpsters were placed all across this section.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where was the injured party and her child? Mark the place.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a broad area, but it should be here [marks]. Yes, roughly there, just next to the dumpsters, 3, 4, 5 metres from the dumpsters. The on-site investigation was very sparse and very difficult to do. We could not access the site in order to investigate, so it boils down to what the UN members were able to do. We did all our work from a distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, according to your conclusions, where did the projectile come from? Can you draw that line?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very difficult to say now where it came from. We did not have the opportunity to see the woman on the site to at least be able to determine -- based on entry and exit wounds, we don't know from which direction -- in which direction the woman was moving with her child. So it's very hard to say anything positive about this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If you can't draw the line, where did the shell come from?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to witness statements, it came from the other side of Miljacka, from this part of Grbavica, according to witness statements. If I draw a line, it would be this [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And who held this area at the end of this line?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the Tito Street, Zmaja od Bosne Street, or across the Miljacka River?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Across the Miljacka River.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The right-hand side was held by the BH Army and the left-hand side by the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At the end of this line, do you recognise the current building of Aero? It used to be the Unioninvest building?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Metalka company building is also there. That should be the direction, but it's hard to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you put number 1 at the site and number 2 next to the Unioninvest building?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Next, number 3 by the Metalka building?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And your date -- and your signature and date?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D901, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, what kind of material clues did you find -- what kind of physical evidence did you find on the site?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was not much physical evidence, apart from blood-stains, a rather large pool of blood, and some sand. That's what we found. We did not find the bodies, just that pool of blood and sand. Now, who covered -- who poured the sand, I don't know. Some reports say that UN representatives poured sand on the site, but we don't know. We did not have access. We could not approach.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were UNPROFOR members there when you were investigating?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that large APC was already placed across the street. We found them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So somebody altered this scene by pouring sand and also water?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was certainly not us, the investigating team. We just described the scene as we found it. Now, who did it? According to witness statements, it was the UN representatives, but it's impossible to say with certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The official report says that the entry wound is on the right-hand side and the exit wound on the left-hand side of the abdomen of Dzenana Sokolovic. Do you want me to call up the document or do you remember it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember it. I don't know from which direction Dzenana was walking, towards Gornji Grad or from down-town towards Cengic Vila. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That was never established, was it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't. And it's difficult to determine the direction of the projectile just on the basis of the entry and exit wounds, because it changes a lot, which direction it came from.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now call up 65 ter 10418.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. We are not getting any translation. Could you repeat your question, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: My question was: How come -- how can you explain that the official report by the investigating commission says that the entry wound is on the right side of the body of Dzenana Sokolovic and the exit wound is on the left side, and in the medical file it's quite the reverse?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, somebody confused this. I believe that my colleague did not describe it accurately, and it was at that time it was very difficult. There was only one pathologist -- one forensic pathologist working. His opinion and his report would have been authoritative about the entry and exit wounds. And the people who were assisting the doctor were not knowledgeable enough to determine which wound was entry and which was exit. That's how the problem occurred.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see page 4 in English and page 5 in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The late Ilijas Dobraca could make a determination about the child, because the child was killed, and the surgeon was to report on Dzenana Sokolovic because he was treating her, and they did report, they did make their determinations. Can we now see page 4 in English and page 3 in Serbian. So you think it's your colleague who was confused about the different sides of the body or the doctors?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to be honest, I would think that it was probably my colleague, rather than the doctor, who made the mistake. Now, when he got the documents and went to the site, or whether he did go there and discuss this with a doctor, because the report was compiled some three months later or so, it is possible that he made that error.
