utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, here we see that this report was prepared on the 19th of November; in other words, on the next day. So if you look at the last paragraph, where it says : "The interview conducted at the Sarajevo KCU, admissions and triage dispensary yielded information that the wounded woman, Dzenana Sokolovic, had received an entry-and-exit wound in the abdominal area and was admitted for treatment at the KCU abdominal clinic. The entry wound was on the right and the exit wound on the left side of the abdomen. The son of Dzenana Sokolovic, Nermin Divovic, aged seven, succumbed to his wounds on the way to hospital and his body was transported to the mortuary. During admission, the doctors established an entry-and-exit wound to the head of the body of Nermin Divovic. The entry wound was at the back of the head, above the right ear, and the exit wound on the face, below the left eye." Is it true that both of them were actually injured or killed by one single shot? One version has it that it had actually exited and wounded the mother, the bullet just went through her, and then hit the child?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there's just one comment here. The only thing that is true is that it killed the child and went through the mother's body.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, but the projectile -- it was determined that the projectile travelled or had this path; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure where the shot -- where the bullet was recovered from. Whether it was found in the mother's body or not, I'm not sure. I can't really say.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now see page 9 of this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here we see the applied treatment of Dzenana. And I believe we need the last page. That's five pages further. Thank you. Now, is this an excerpt from the protocol on the examination and autopsy of the body, where it says that this is a blast injury, that the entry wound was on the right cheek and the exit wound on the left side of the head, in the back, and it was signed by Dr. Ilijas Dobraca, whereas on the previous page we see that the path of this shot or this projectile was described in the reverse; correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, it was that the entry is at the back of the head and the exit on the right-hand -- on the right cheek.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, is it true that it was not properly established, the trajectory of the path, the bullet canal, and the place where the victims were?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, here we cannot really determine the orientation. We could not determine it because we -- they weren't on site. But the only thing we could go by was the witness statements. And based on the information that we can see, that were written down, in fact, there are some discrepancies, and I agree that it is difficult to determine exactly what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you agree that in peacetime, your work conditions were far better and that you had all the necessary parameters in order to establish the facts because you were able to actually find the injured parties on the site, itself?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, and based on that it was possible to determine the direction from which the projectile had come. That's something that it was possible to do in peacetime, but in wartime we also had occasion to proceed like that. But in this particular case, that was impossible.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the speakers please not overlap or not follow so soon one after the other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You are advised again by the interpreters to put a pause.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I thought I was speaking -- or I am speaking Serbian, and Mr. Besic Bosnian, which would mean that two different languages are spoken. But apparently we are speaking the same language.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, all that matters is that we can understand each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let me ask this -- oh, may I ask whether these documents that we've just shown under these numbers and the pages that we indicated -- I would actually like to tender them, so can I ask whether they've been admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I believe they're in as P459, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Then we can remove it from the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, let us go back to Markale II, the incident of 28th of August, 1995. You took part in preparing this sketch. Could we please have 65 ter 09899 on the screens. Can you recognise this cover page? We see also Salko Cerimagic's name there?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have page 3 in Serbian, and I believe it's the same page in English. Perhaps we can only have the English version before us. Thank you. Can we rotate it, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, could you indicate on this sketch where the north bearing is? You can see the tram tracks; right? You can recognise that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, certainly I can.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I ask some assistance, please. We need the pen, the electronic pen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think we are having some technical difficulties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The electronic pen does not seem to work at this moment. Could we do something else, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. In that case -- well, may I just ask, can we revisit this sketch later on? Apparently, that will be possible. Then we'll move on to something else and then get back to this later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you -- have you ever seen the portion of the video-clip that was made before you arrived on the crime scene?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you're asking about the video-clip we saw yesterday, I had occasion to see it on TV earlier on. There were several journalists there and -- who were filming all this, and later on it was shown and broadcast in the main news programme.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, do you have any explanation as to how a TV Sarajevo journalist happened to be on-site just at the time of the incident?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't think that they were on-site, themselves. I think they received this video material also from some foreign journalists, and these people roamed the streets all the time, so -- in order to be able to film the events. I think that's how it was done.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now see P1450. That is a video-clip. It was admitted as P1450, so can we see it from 3:28 to 3:35.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see it one more time, please? Right here, let's stay here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, can you see here that we have quite a few uniformed persons, and apparently they're wearing military uniforms here in this frame? We can see that; correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can see that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have -- could we now admit this particular frame, 1D2859, and get a number for it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it possible to capture this image and keep it as a separate still image?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: They say it's not possible.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We do have our own still. That's 1D2859.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well, we'll up-load that, 1D2859.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we rotate it so that we can see it in full.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is the same still, but now it appears as a still image. Is it true -- is it correct that these people are outside the northerly entrance to the market-place?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you now please mark, approximately, on this still, the point of impact where the shell landed, knowing that the entrance is facing north?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure it has been fixed. Shall we give -- shall we give it a try? No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, I thought it had been fixed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can tell you that the man standing with the blue top, and where these two uniformed men are standing, that is where the point of impact was.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In other words, the man in the blue -- in the dark blue or kind of navy blue top, he is standing close to the centre of the explosion?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and these two soldiers.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. In that case, could we please admit this photo into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you try to mark it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you please date this photo?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And we know from the transcript that approximately where you put the circle, that's where the centre of the explosion was. Well, we can see -- I'm not going to count them all, but we can see there are five to six soldiers in this photo; correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you. There are five, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know who these soldiers are? What unit did they belong to?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have no idea. And I can just say what I said yesterday, the market, Markale, was an open-type market and anyone could go buy whatever they needed, so I do not rule out that these soldiers went there to perhaps buy or sell cigarettes, or lighters, or something like that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like to tender this, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It will be admitted as ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D902, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 09899, 65 ter, page 3, the sketch. Can we revisit that, the sketch that we had before us a moment ago. Could you please just wait for the pen to be active. Yes, here now we have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you please mark north, once you can -- once you have the pen?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And indicate with an arrow what the direction of north would be.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, here we see the town market. Would you please indicate number 1 -- with a number 1 the building where the market is?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, would you please indicate the northern entrance outside of which the shell landed?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Put the number 2 there, please.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, can you please place the point of impact?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. President, all of this is explained in the legend provided with this sketch. This is a complete repetition of that information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think so, but we could up-load it, the English version, as originally suggested by the accused. It's all marked there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, could we then have the legend before us, too, so that we can just have the witness confirm it. Can we split the screen and then show the legend on one half of the screen and this sketch on the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we wait for this: Mr. Besic, you said earlier today that the stabiliser was how far from the point of impact, the center of the explosion?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean where we found it and took photos?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, where you established that it was in your investigation.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was some 45 to 50 metres from the -- from the scene, and I said that it was possible that it was -- it is possible that a stabiliser may be a bit off, a bit away from the center of the explosion, a metre or so to one side or the other.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have the legend, please. This is not quite that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So number 1 is the place of impact; right? Number 2, a body part, a right foot, and so on and so forth. Then number 6 is the motorbike?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 7 and 8, we have "child's canvas shoe" and then "left hand."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we see the next page of the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Under 12, we see the stabiliser. Could you now please put a circle around number 12?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the place where the projectile was recovered [marks]. And because you come from Sarajevo, you know that this is where the Vlasic store was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. Now, was it recovered on the pavement?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was found right outside the store that I just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please put a number 1 there -- or, rather, put a circle around the number 1 that we already have indicated on the sketch.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That is the point of impact; correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Well, please date and sign this photo, and then we can move on to the next one.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to admit -- to tender this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D903, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But, again, I really don't see the point of this exercise. It's already there, number 12.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but I would like for us to be able to establish, finally, where the stabiliser was recovered from. We have all kinds of information, ranging from 5 metres to 40 metres, and then later on we will see that there are other attempts to tamper with the stabiliser. Now, as for the new photo that we got from this witness, we could see that the stabiliser was on the roadway and that that is where it was filmed by UNPROFOR members, and we will see that there's a whole Rashomon story here about this stabiliser, all kinds of different versions. Now, could we see P1450 from 3:52 to 3:54. This is a video-clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And let me ask you, Witness, whether there were any military installations or any troops in that area? Now can you see, Witness, would you take a look at this. Is this just another --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused please repeat the question. The interpreter could not hear the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. The interpreters didn't hear your previous question, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The first question was whether there were any troops in this area and whether there were any military installations nearby.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that there were any military units deployed there in the very center. I said yesterday that there were some at the military hall, the one-time military hall, and right here we see that there is a soldier or a police officer carrying a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And how far is this from where the troops were deployed?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think some 400 to 500 metres. There's a park in between and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you mean four to five football fields?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think 400 to 500 metres, that would be a stadium away.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, could we please play this video on so that we can show that this is actually a soldier, because soldiers wore green uniforms and the police had blue ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, but there were also some camouflage uniforms. At this time, there already were camouflage uniforms for the police as well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So first we see one soldier, and then we see another one appearing in this footage. Can we go back to 1D2860, 1D2860. I would like that to be shown, and then I would like to tender it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you agree, Mr. Besic, that this doorway or entrance that we see here is, in fact, the doorway or entrance to a building called "Semberija"?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean where the soldier is standing?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no. As I mentioned earlier, that is the Vlasic store. That's what it used to be. Now, across the street from that is Semberija. You see where you can see the wall pocked and some markings there. They were damaged by bullets and fragments.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, do you know that the Semberija building was used by the BH Army as a quarter-master storage area?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know that it was used as a bakery and that they made bread there for units and so on. It was a bakery, basically. But the fact that it was used by members of the army or the police, well, they used it in order to get their bread there, because that's where the bread was baked and distributed from.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now, can we have a still, 1D2860. Can we have that still or that photo on the screen, please. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, would you please indicate on this photo -- or could you actually date it and sign it? Or, rather, can we tender this without the witness's signature? Is it necessary?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think his signature is necessary. We'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D904, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just for your information, that you'll have an hour left.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. That is why I'm going to skip some questions. And we will now look at 1D2863, please. And with your permission, after the break, after we look at the new material that we received yesterday, we would like to put the rest of our questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In this photo, does this green rectangle cover the place of the explosion?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This place was not filmed or photographed before cleaning; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph, this panoramic shot, was taken after the cleaning and after the debris was removed from the place of the centre of the explosion. When I got into this building, I made this panoramic shot by taking four separate shots and putting them together. So in this panoramic shot, you can see that the material has already been cleaned and that the damage on the asphalt has already been marked in chalk.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Before cleaning, there is no photograph or recording, is that correct, only after cleaning; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, after cleaning.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I believe that this has already been admitted, so it's not necessary to tender it. Can we now look at P1450 from 6:47 to 7:02, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think this compilation, as it is shown now, has never been admitted, and I don't think that this is what the witness has produced. Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's correct, this hasn't been admitted. The green section, I believe, has been placed there by the Karadzic Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And I see the stamps on the picture. And this is compiled by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, from pages taken from the photo file relating to Markale II, as far as I can see. Mr. Karadzic can surely confirm that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: As such, it is never admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, that means it wasn't. I thought that was already admitted. These are photographs from the photo documentation. We placed them one next to the other. We didn't fit in the margins of the sidewalk, as the witness managed to do. But the fact is that the place of impact is below this green rectangle and that you cannot see it in any of these photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And we can see, on the photograph on the left-hand side, that this was taken before cleaning; is that correct? You can see how much material there is left here?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. It wasn't possible to fit it in. You can see that all of it was photographed from one apartment, from one angle, so it's not done properly. You didn't fit it in correctly. Yesterday's panoramic shot actually showed the actual state of the scene as we found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm waiting for the translation. Let me ask you this: On the left photograph, do you consider this scene to be cleaned?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't clean the scene. We cleaned only the crater, the place where the explosion of the mortar shell actually exploded. We did not clean the rest. It's not part of our job, to clean that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. We're not going to admit this, not to over-burden the case file. Can we look at the film P14 -- P1450.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, Mr. Besic, that the stabiliser is being observed by the UNPROFOR investigators while it is still on the roadway?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you have an explanation why this stabiliser is found in different places in different investigative material?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do have the explanation as follows: When we came to the scene, we photographed from two directions, from the direction of Bascarsija and from the direction of Marin Dvor. In both those photographs, you can see the projectile next to the shop that we mentioned, Vlasic. How the UN members -- and what they did here, I don't know. I was a little bit surprised when I saw this footage. When you compare my photographs and when you compare the photographs of the work and the measurements made by the UNPROFOR members, you will see that that is, more or less, right across from the entrance, where the projectile was placed. I don't know who actually put it there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we tender this excerpt of the footage? Can we have 1D2732, please. That is a still. We would like to tender that. 1D2732.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D905, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now give the stabiliser to the witness, the one that we have here, while we still have the photograph of the stabiliser on the monitor. This is Exhibit P1454.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you now tell us if you agree that the actual body of the stabiliser is very eroded and that you can see -- or corroded, and that you can see this corrosion on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can see some traces of that, but I think that that is not actually so. When you look at the fins, that would be the only criteria in evaluating the state of the stabiliser. It could be some soil or something else that appears to be damage to the body, but I think that the actual fins are the only criteria.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, if you give me a new stabiliser and some pliers, I can make it look just like this one here. But tell me, how long did it take for the shell to fly and hit its target?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be very difficult to get a new stabiliser into this state only with the use of pliers. That would take a very long time. I don't know if this is soil, or sand, or something that was on the body of the stabiliser, but I think in order to identify the stabiliser, you would need to look only at the fins, the shape or distribution of the fins, and I wouldn't dare to identify a projectile only on the basis of the residual soil found on the body of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If the crater was shallow, as your photographs indicate, then we would have to assume that the stabiliser did not embed itself below the surface?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. After the contact and the explosion --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Objection. These are questions relating to ballistics. The witness has repeatedly stated that he has no particular expertise in ballistics. These questions can be directed towards an expert witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, but the witness volunteered to answer. I agree with you, Mr. Gaynor. But in the meantime, shall we put it on the ELMO so that we can take a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we are waiting: Witness, sir, you are stating that it could possibly be soil. We think that this is quite substantial corrosion or erosion which could not have been created on a dead object. Can you please explain to us, what is the difference between these two objects?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really don't see any difference between the two. We can interpret this --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Again, objection, Mr. President. These questions are going to the cause of the deformation at the end of the stabiliser. Of course, the stabiliser, in the nanoseconds before it is shot back, is subjected to massive force. Now, the exact cause of the markings on the stabiliser is a question for expert evidence, not for this witness, in my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I think you exhausted this question in relation to this witness. I think this witness has answered as far as he can.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. But there is still the question of whether this is the same stabiliser, the one that you're holding in your hand, and the one that was filmed by the French investigators.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that, in your opinion, the same stabiliser?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's the identical one.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have 1D2864 now, please. You can keep the stabiliser, because compared to the one on the photograph, there are significant differences on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Before we go any further, I'd like to clarify for the record that the yellow lines we see on this exhibit have been placed there by the Karadzic Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it to be the case. Let's move on, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please say if you recognise the place of the initial fuse and the two holes which are essentially on the same line as the main large hole?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If we compare the left and the right photographs, they are identical, and the middle one was probably photographs -- photographed at a specific angle and was probably tilted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You described to the Chamber what these three holes are, the three holes on the stabiliser?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know what the middle one is. It's the initial cap. I don't know what the other two are. I'm not a ballistics expert, but the assumption is that it could be -- these are the openings in order to place the primary charge into the stabiliser.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Your assumption is quite correct. These are the tool openings that are used to screw the primary charge into the body of the stabiliser.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, the interpreters couldn't hear your last part -- the last part of your answer. Could you repeat it, kindly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the former JNA, where I served in the army, I was the one who was calculating the targets. This is a specialty that dealt with determining the firing from 120-millimetre and 155-millimetre guns, so I am quite familiar with this particular kind of ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the position of these holes, in relation to the fins, varies? All of this is from the photo documentation. The right one is a video still. The middle one is what you are holding in your hand.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the left one, you can see, is actually not standing on its own, but somebody is supporting it with a stick or something in order to be able to look at the markings. So that immediately means that the angle of the openings is different. But I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If we were to say that this is a clock, for example, on the first photograph the line dissects it immediately after 12.00, between 6.00 and 7.00; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but you can see that the stabiliser is held in the lower right-hand corner by an object, so that means that the angle is changed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But the constant reference point are the fins. That is not changed. Nobody can change it.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the first one and the right one are identical. The left photograph and the right photograph, the position is identical in relation to the fins.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But the one you have in front of you is not identical?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The middle one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The middle photograph is a photograph of the object you have in front of you.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and it's even more at an angle. I don't know how that happened. I am talking about the artefacts that were found on the scene. The left photograph was photographed at the scene, the right photograph was also made at the scene, and you can see, by the position of the holes, that they are identical in relation to the fins. And the middle photograph was filmed somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the middle photograph is the photograph of the object that you have in front of you?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, could you repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The left photograph and the right photograph are in the same position, and the yellow arrow indicates that they're in the same position, and they were taken at the scene. The middle photograph, I really cannot say how the whole object is tilted in this particular way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The middle photograph is a photograph of the exhibit that we have here in the courtroom, the physical object; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The ELMO is not working. Yes. Could you hold this --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can just make an assumption.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- so that we can see the holes. Yes. What is your assumption, Mr. Besic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I assume that when the stabiliser came to the premises of the criminal lab, it was taken by the Counter-Sabotage Unit, and it's possible that they did unscrew it, make some kind of rotation. But I guarantee that this is the actual stabiliser from Markale II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we admit these three photographs?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D906, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We would now desire to have the break in order for us to be able to prepare to show the material that we received yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll have a break and resume at 10 to 12.00 -- 10 to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like to ask for everyone's patience so that we can look through the video footage that we received with this witness. Can we play from 12:09 -- actually, 12:06. This video system here does not have the same counter time that is on the actual footage, on the actual machine, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What is the 65 ter number for this or exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We reported it as 1D2867, 2867. This is the footage that we received yesterday because the witness was kind enough to bring it, and the Prosecution disclosed it yesterday.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this was already admitted as Exhibit 896. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does that mean that the whole footage was admitted, not its parts; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, the whole footage was admitted. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, can I ask you to tell us where the center of the explosion here is in relation to the position of the cameraman?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's to the right side. The cameraman, that's me, the person with the camera in a white T-shirt.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. You are the person in the white T-shirt. What about the person who is filming? They are standing behind the market?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he's standing between -- from the north, he's standing on the right-hand side of the market, because on the right side of the market, there is a street that leads to Vase Miskina. This is from the left-hand side, looking to the right entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So the center of the explosion is below this person that is hidden behind the pole?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You do not see the center of the explosion because it is hidden by this light pole.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the Usher's assistance now and activate the pen. Okay, excuse me, this is the video footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, can you see on this facade this damage?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the facade damaged up to a height of 3 metres, and this indicates precisely the direction from which the projectile came. That fragmented a large -- and caused a lot of damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you see, on this pole, the damage?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You don't see it from this side, because the projectile dropped from the other side. There is a possibility that there is damage. It's possible that the damage could also have been prevented by bodies that came between the pole and the shrapnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about the yellow facade. Do you see the damage on the yellow facade and the side of the pole facing the cameraman?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can see some damage on the wall. But if you're thinking of the yellow facade, it's possible that the shrapnel ricocheted and caused this damage, but it could also be some kind of old damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: From an earlier explosion?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do we have an investigation of this earlier explosion?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really don't know. There were many explosions. It's very difficult to remember something like that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the team -- the UNPROFOR team that conducted the investigation on the scene at the same time as you did?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these are the UNPROFOR members, and we can see people here from the federal MUP also. We can see the operatives. I am in the right-hand corner, the person who's photographing the center of impact where the number 1 is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And who's the person who is cleaning?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one is cleaning. I cleaned it. This is me. I am the one who's cleaning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we see Lieutenant-Colonel Konings in this photograph, in this footage -- in this still?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did anybody interfere with your investigation at that time? Was there any kind of pressure by the masses, were there any problems?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there were no problems. It wasn't possible to create problems. The scene was secured. Nobody could enter. You understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let us continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Let me just interrupt for a second. No objection to the admission of this video. This video has not, in fact, been admitted so far. And, secondly, we have no objection to its admission, but in order to make the record clear, Mr. Karadzic should call out the time or the minutes and seconds for each of the frames that we're observing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So I was wondering whether the exhibit that we admitted as D896 was kind of a still from this image, from this video, which were admitted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So when we admitted D896, it's limited to that part which was shown at the time, I take it. So we need to -- then you don't have any objection to the admission of the whole video?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then there's no objection. We admit it as D896.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And if the Defence would kindly offer the Chamber and the Prosecution the time slots of each video shown in the courtroom. Having said that, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. But, you see, it's easier to use this clock on the camera, because the software we are using to display this is completely different to the software that we have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's fine, but we have to note those numbers into the transcript so that we can follow at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, Mr. Besic, that this investigating team of the UNPROFOR was shown this stabiliser on the road next to the tracks?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's clearly evident here, and it's accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it the one-and-only stabiliser in this incident?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, only one.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We were at 12 minutes, 45 seconds at the time. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm afraid this is 12:55 on the clock. I don't know what it is on the software.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the same stabiliser marked by your investigating team with number 12 and also marked with "12" in the sketch?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We can play back the movie.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So where we broadcast the image, we'll not broadcast that. Let's move on, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see 65 ter 09899, page 3, which is the sketch, and then the key to the sketch. Next page in English, please. Next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If you look at this, we see number 12. There is no number 13. In these other two places, in the middle of the tracks and in the road where you recorded the stabiliser, can you mark these two spots on the sketch?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was that number 13?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then put "13" there.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When the Frenchmen were filming, where was it; in the middle of the road?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The identical spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I don't think so. What you were photographing was closer to the tracks, the railroad. We can play it again, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's approximately the same place, perhaps a metre or two away. I can mark it like this, if you wish [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then put it as "12A," because the previous one was "12."

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In different witness statements, there are discrepancies between 15 and 40 metres. Don't you think there are too many "if"s and "but"s about this crime scene?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know that it could be a difference between 25 metres and 40, because there is a width of the market, and then the width of the pavement, then the road. You can see exactly how far it is from number 12 to number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Put your signature there, please, and the date.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Besic, I thank you, and I hope you'll have no hard feelings, because I'm only after the truth, and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This last marked sketch will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D907, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before you, Mr. Gaynor, Judge Baird will ask a question of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, we shall like some clarification on an answer you gave when you were dealing with Markale I earlier today. Now, Dr. Karadzic asked you: "Would the shell have been activated on contact with a stall roofing?" And you answered to the effect: "Since it is plastic, I am sure -- I am sure that it would have -- I think that it would have. But it did not touch any roofing. It just landed like that. It could have touched this iron roof, but it did not land there. It landed where it landed." Now, would the shell have been activated on contact with the stall roofing? Can you help us with it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if it hit only the plastic roof, I doubt it. But if it hit the iron part of the roofing, yes, it would activate, certainly. However, there was no contact, and the point of contact, the point of impact is on the tarmac between the stalls.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, I'm going to ask you a couple of questions about the sniping of Dzenana Sokolovic. Earlier on today, Mr. Karadzic drew your attention to a discrepancy in the official report, as he described it, by the Investigation Commission. Mr. Karadzic said that that report says that the entry wound is on the right side of the body of Dzenana Sokolovic and the exit wound is on the left side, and in the medical file, it's quite the reverse. Your answer was: "Yes, somebody was confused by this. I believe that my colleague did not describe it accurately and that it was at that time very difficult." Later on, Dr. Karadzic asked you: "So you think it's your colleague who was confused about the different sides of the body or the doctors?" And your answer was: "Well, to be honest, I would think that it was probably my colleague, rather than the doctor, who made the mistake." Do you recall that exchange of questions and answers?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember most of it. There is a discrepancy between the findings of a pathologist in the clinical centre, the pathologist Dobraca, and the forensic pathologist who received the body of the body and examined it. Dobraca noted that the entry wound was around the eye and the entry -- and the exit close to the right ear, whereas the medics who received him at Kosevo said --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry to interrupt, Mr. Besic. You remember that the examining physician was Sefik Beslic?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I did not see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Besic, in the documentation shown to you by Mr. Karadzic, it states that the examining physician was Sefik Beslic. And I'd now like to call up P472, and if we could go to page 2 in the English and page 3 in the B/C/S. The document that is coming up is the witness statement of Sefik Beslic, which is dated 30th January 2007, which has been admitted pursuant to Rule 92 bis. I can read the relevant paragraphs, if Your Honour wishes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We can follow our own computer. The Usher's computer has been frozen for some unidentifiable reasons, so let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, I'm going to read to you two short paragraphs from a statement made by Dr. Beslic on the 30th of January, 2007, which now appears --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we have it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: It now appears.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, if you look at the paragraphs in front of you, and if you could focus, really, on paragraphs 4 and 5. And tell us when you've had a chance to read those to yourself.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've read this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you now able to comment on whether you believe your colleague or the doctor was the person who made the error at the time of the incident?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe my colleague could have made that statement. But we note that the statement of Pathologist Ilijas Dobraca is not consistent with the finding of this physician.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Besic, if we can just bring up P459, page 3 in the English. Page 10 in the B/C/S, please. Sorry, it's the fifth page in the English. This is a record of the examination of Dzenana Sokolovic, and the record states that the entry point of the wound -- sorry, it should be 8 in the English, please. The previous page, please. The conclusion of the examining physician was that the entry point of the wound was 0.5 centimetres' wide to the paramedian left bleeding, and the exit point of the wound, 3 by 2 centimetres, to the paramedian right and bleeding. Now, in the statement of Dr. Beslic, which we've just inspected, he says that: "I can now state that without doubt, the bullet which wounded Dzenana Sokolovic entered the right side of her abdomen and exited on the left side of her abdomen."

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these two documents coincide. After all, this is a specialised doctor, a surgeon. And having seen these two documents, he probably confirmed the finding that the entry is on the left side and exit on the right side.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I just ask Mr. Gaynor to say when this new finding was made, because the entry wound in this finding is smaller than the exit wound. When was this statement made, and to whom, this new statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's the 92 bis statement admitted already in this case?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, it's been admitted as P472 in this case. I can move on, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Can you tell us when that statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. It was the 30th of January, 2007. And the examination of Dzenana Sokolovic, according to the statement, took place on the 30th of January, 2007.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We can move on, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, the second --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just add why the Defence is opposed to 92 bis? This is a very important witness, and we are opposed to 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's admitted. There may be further ways to bring that issue before the Chamber on your part. It's for the Defence case. Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The second subject, Mr. Besic, which I'm going to ask you about is the Markale I incident site. Now, we heard questions by Mr. Karadzic today, and he showed you footage and stills of footage of an artificial leg at the Markale I incident site. And he said today, at page 28: "This was broadcast on Muslim television. We see the artificial leg here that was left at this place." Mr. Karadzic has previously asserted, for the Court's information, at page 2322 that the artificial leg was planted at the incident location following the explosion. Now, I'd like to call up a video, please. This is 65 ter 40109, and I'm going to play several clips from this. The first clip is from 03:45 to 03:49.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: You see the artificial leg in that clip, Mr. Besic?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The second clip is from 8 minutes to 8 minutes and 10 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: You see the artificial leg again in that clip?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can see the prosthesis.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could we now play 10 minutes and 20 seconds to 10 minutes and 30 -- 10 minutes and 29 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I think you can see it again there, Mr. Besic. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: For the final clip, I'd like you to listen very carefully to the voices that you can hear. Could we play from 24 minutes and 40 seconds to 25 minutes and 10 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Were you able to hear the voices in that clip?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, there's no need to give a precise transcript of what they were saying, but what -- to what effect were the words that you heard?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, people were very bitter over the -- over what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We did not receive an interpretation of the words on the video. Could you tell us what the people were saying?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is spoken in revolt by the people who happened to be there on the scene, insulting words. You see that one of these people threw the prosthesis into the air and said, Take this to Karadzic. And I really wouldn't like to repeat the rest.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence kindly asks the Chamber to receive the transcript of this, because staging/orchestration is referred to. Can you please tell the Trial Chamber the man said, Take this to Karadzic to see how we orchestrate things?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no. It's -- the context is completely different. He said, Take this to Karadzic, because they seem to think we are orchestrating things.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We can replay it and ask the interpreters to give the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We'll replay that clip. It is from 24 minutes and 40 seconds to 25 minutes and 10 seconds.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "At 12.30 in the broader area around Markale Market, it killed a lot of our fellow citizens and wounded many. We repeat again that the Clinical Centre of Kosevo is still receiving the dead and the wounded, so that the Clinical Centre still does not have figures about the wounded and dead. "Fuck Karadzic. They say that we are staging things, we staging things. Fuck his mother."

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Besic, on the basis of your observations of the incident location on the day of the incident, and on the basis of your viewing of this video, can you tell the Court whether you received any information to suggest that the artificial limb was placed at the site following the explosion?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were all sorts of speculations and stories, but I think this belongs to a man. And I'm sorry that our colleagues at the mortuary did not fit the prosthesis back to the body and photographed it. In view of the circumstances and all that happened, we were not able to do everything, but it's a fact that this artificial limb was not placed subsequently. It belonged to a person who was actually injured.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That ends the redirect examination. I'd like to tender those four clips that were played.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In separate pieces?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We can -- yes, as separate exhibit numbers, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The Registry will assign numbers in due course, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then that concludes your evidence, Mr. Besic. The Chamber would like to thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it. Now you are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you wait a minute until we draw the curtain so that you can leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And at the same time, we'll bring in the next witness. Now I think you can leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Goodbye to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: There's one housekeeping matter, Mr. President, that will take about 30 seconds, if I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, after we open the curtain.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I would just like to ask if we could have a brief pause, no more than five minutes at maximum, for the purpose of logistics of switching computers before the next witness comes in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'll just raise that one point I was going to raise, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: On the 5th of November, 2010, at the end of the redirect examination of Emir Turkusic, Your Honours asked for information regarding a video-clip which we played during the redirect examination. Mr. Karadzic, in fact, asked for it, and Your Honours asked me to provide it. The video is P1933. The location of the clip was the Lion Cemetery in Sarajevo. The date of the recording was the 11th of June, 1992. The journalist was Jeremy Bowen. The television company is the BBC. And by way of supplementary information, the incident is described in paragraph 7 of Mr. Bowen's statement -- amalgamated statement, which will be tendered in due course. That's 65 ter 22660. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. While Ms. Edgerton sets her computer on, can we deal with administrative matters in the meantime? You can do that, you can start right now. We are seized of the 65 ter motion -- no, the motion to amend the 65 ter witness list, to which the Defence does not oppose, so that will be granted. But in that response, I remember the Defence asked for the list of all the remaining witnesses in the order of calling, but I don't think there has been any practice to be given a list of all witnesses in the calling -- in the order of the calling. Our practice is to receive the order of witnesses bimonthly. Does it not suffice, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, actually, Mr. President, from time to time the Prosecution has responded to disclosure motions. They indicate that this witness is the 240th witness in their list, and so they have that information. We wouldn't hold it to them -- wouldn't hold them to it, but it would be very helpful to us, because we have to start reviewing prior testimonies and statements of witnesses well in advance. And from the municipality's case, for example, we have no idea if we're going to hear witnesses from Sanski Most in 2011 or 2012, and we just -- it would be a lot easier if we had some -- at least a tentative idea of which order in which the witnesses would be coming.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I thought your concern was that the Defence does not want to waste time preparing the -- preparing for the Prosecution witness, who the Prosecution then goes on to drop from their list.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, we already know which ones are active on the list right now. And it would be helpful to have, actually, a consolidated list, because they've been dropping people from time to time and it's been difficult to keep track of that. So that was one motivation. But it would also be useful, if they are going to give a list, that it be in some kind of order of which they're being called.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But we are not seized of that motion, as such. But speaking for myself, bimonthly witness orders may be sufficient at this time. And for the further purpose, you can contact the Prosecution, and the Prosecution will co-operate, without any doubt.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you need to pause for five minutes or three minutes? Shall we -- yes, we'll break for five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll resume at quarter to 2:00.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: May I -- before -- before we start, may I introduce Aleksandar Stefanovic, replacing Mr. Sladojevic, who is not completely in good health. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon, Mr. Stefanovic. Yes, Ms. Edgerton -- before that, good afternoon, Mr. Djozo. If you could stand and take the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, and thank you for the indulgence earlier of five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, could you state your full name for the record, please?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: My name is Nedzib Djozo.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djozo. Now, do you recall, Mr. Djozo, giving two statements in the past to representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor for this Tribunal, one in November 1995 and the second one in April 2005?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And do you also recall that after this, you testified before this Tribunal on two previous occasions, first in the trial of Dragomir Milosevic in 2007 and the second time during the trial of Momcilo Perisic in 2009?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, on Tuesday, 7 December, in preparation for your testimony here today, did you sign a further statement consolidating and clarifying the evidence you've presented over the course of the last years?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: I did sign that statement, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And did this statement also contain, reference and discuss a number of documents and photographs?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Before signing that statement, was it read back to you in a language you understood?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, if you were asked the same questions today which gave rise to the evidence contained in that statement you signed on 7 December, would you give the same answers?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes, I would give the same answers.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. In that case, Your Honours, could I ask that Mr. Djozo's amalgamated statement of 7 December 2010, 65 ter 90206, be marked as the next Prosecution exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit P1978, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll now read a summary of the written evidence of Mr. Djozo. During the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Mr. Nedzib Djozo served as a police officer for the Sarajevo Police Department in the Old Town, or Stari Grad, police Station. In his capacity as police investigator, he investigated many shelling and sniping cases. Mr. Djozo conducted a number of on-site investigations concerning the wounding and killing of civilians in Sedrenik, a residential area under the responsibility of his police station. In these investigations, he found that the fire was coming from Bosnian Serb-held territory, in particular the sniping location of Spicasta Stijena, which is a hill overlooking the Sedrenik neighbourhood. In the months immediately before the shelling of the Markale Marketplace on 28 August 1995, Mr. Djozo investigated several incidents of mortar impacts in the immediate vicinity. His investigations on all these incidents showed that all shells were fired from Bosnian Serb-held territories. On the day of the Markale Market incident, he attended on site with the injured and killed. Mr. Djozo was a member of the team that investigated the shelling of the Bascarsija flea market on 22 December 1994. He was at the scene, and his task was to assist the investigative judge, who was leading the investigation, with locating traces from the explosion. During the course of his investigations, Mr. Djozo encountered other explosive devices that were used against or fired on Sarajevo. He investigated a modified air-bomb that fell in the canyon of the Moscenice River without exploding. He found that was an air-bomb with four rocket motors attached to it, and he recalls that 90 kilos of explosive was removed from the bomb. Based on his knowledge that the Bosnian Army did not have such devices, he came to the conclusion that the bomb was fired from Bosnian Serb-held territory. Mr. Djozo also saw gas containers filled with explosives which were rolled down into the city from Bosnian Serb-held territories on the slopes of Mount Trebevic beneath Osmice. That's the summary of the written evidence. And if I may, I'll move to some questions in relation to parts of that written evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Djozo, in your amalgamated statement that you signed earlier this week, you noted that you were injured in a shelling during the summer of 1993 and that the incident took place in front of your police station. That's at paragraph 8 of that statement. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I can't recall the exact date. I know it was summer. I was in my summer uniform with a short-sleeved shirt. Somewhere between 1100 and 1300 hours, as I was standing outside the Stari Grad Police Station, all of a sudden the building next-door was hit by a mortar shell. My colleague, who was standing outside the station, guarding the parking-lot, was told by me to run for cover because another shell might be coming shortly. As I was uttering those words, the next shell hit the front of the adjoining building, and the detonation literally threw me into the police station. Disoriented completely, I went down into the basement. I was followed by several colleagues who were also injured. I was injured in my arm and my leg. A colleague of mine, who was about 20, 30 metres down from the station, was more seriously wounded. He was hit by shrapnel in the legs as he was coming in to work. After this, we were transported to the Kosevo Hospital, where we were given medical assistance. My injuries were not serious, and I was released home immediately.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Djozo, if we were to show you a map just to orient everyone, would you be able to indicate where we might find the Stari Grad Police Station on the map?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes, I could.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we see, then, P00815, page 7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Probably we need to zoom in further.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And it's page 7 that we need. Your indulgence for a moment. I'm advised this image has only one page. We'll see, as quickly as we can, what we can do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If this is of a high quality, we can -- oh, no, it's not.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I think I can do one better, Your Honour, if I can just beg your indulgence for a moment. The proper number, I'm advised, is 09390C, and it would be page 7 of that 65 ter 09390C. That's sheet 5. Could we move over two to sheet 7, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Djozo, do you see a map cut-out on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to look at this map cut-out in preparation for your preparation today?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: What do you recognise it to be?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: This is a part of the city of Sarajevo, Stari Grad and part of the center.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we zoom in a little bit, please, on the two bottom right-hand squares of this map.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Djozo, then, on this map, are you able to identify the location of the Stari Grad Police Station, where you were at the time of the incident you just described?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: The Stari Grad Police Station is in 10 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the name of the street.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Approximately where the letter I is on the right-hand side of the street.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could you just repeat the street name, please, Mr. Djozo?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: It's in Lugavina Street, number 10 [marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Marking the location of the Stari Grad Police Station with a red dot or circle. Now, could you estimate the approximate distance between this location and the scene of the Markale II shelling incident?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Lugavina Street is approximately five metres' wide. The first shell hit the building facing the Police Administration of Stari Grad, and it came from the direction of Lapisnica. The second shell hit the building just opposite Stari Grad Police Station, some 3 metres away from the tarmac, from road level, towards the first floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: How far is the Stari Grad Police Station from the scene of Markale II?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Roughly, less than 1 kilometre, more than 500 metres, in Mula Mustafe Baseskije Street. So between 500 and a thousand metres [marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And have you marked that second location with a cross -- a red cross just now?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: With respect to the day you were injured, had there been any shelling, shooting, or other military activity in the area, to your recollection?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: I don't recall that there was any shooting, any combat. And that was the most dangerous thing to us in town. After complete quiet, there would come a shell injuring and killing and maiming the citizens of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Do you recall any -- seeing any weapons placements, unit positions, headquarters, or any other military objects or troops in the area of where you were injured?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
