utterances.text: In the area where I was wounded, there is not a single structure used by the army. The only structure of that kind is the police station. Nearby, there was a kindergarten that was destroyed, so that, too, was empty. Most of the buildings are residential.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could this be the next Prosecution exhibit, please, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall I ask the witness to date and put his signature on this?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I sign this initial anywhere?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. And today is the 9th of December, 2010. And your initial, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1979, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Djozo, in your statement, at paragraphs 16 to 18, you described the location called Spicasta Stijena and the surrounding area. You said it was, and I quote. "... a hill dominant, overlooking the Sedrenik neighbourhood." And further you said: "Below Spicasta Stijena, there is a rock, and there is meadow [Realtime transcript read in error "metal"] under that." Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: I don't know what kind of metal --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It should read "meadow."

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Indeed, "meadow."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. Spicasta Stijena is an elevation overlooking the Sedrenik neighbourhood. It's built up only with houses. Private houses were built there, and Spicasta Stijena overlooks these houses. It's about 50 to 100 metres' high. It's bare rock. It's practically a cliff, very difficult to climb. The only route that could take you there was a road that went around Spicasta Stijena on the right-hand side, and that road also led to Barice neighbourhood, which was behind Spicasta Stijena. From Barice neighbourhood, if you took that road further, you would get to Biosko and Crepoljsko settlements.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Perhaps I could stop you there and ask you to look at a photograph, if I may. 65 ter 09999, page 50. Pardon me, 15.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Do you see the photo on the screen in front of you, Mr. Djozo?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes, I see the photo.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And did you see this photograph in preparation for your testimony here today?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Do you recognise it, then? Can you tell us what it shows?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: It shows Spicasta Stijena and the neighbourhood underneath.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, does this accurately depict the area as you knew it to be during the war?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes, it looked exactly like that during the war. Maybe not all the roofs were there. Some roofs were destroyed, but the rest is the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: If we could move on to another photograph, then, 65 ter 09999, page 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Similarly, Mr. Djozo, have you seen this photo in preparation for your testimony today?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen the photo.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Do you recognise it? And if so, could you tell us what it represents?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes. These houses are parts of Sedrenik, which lies to the right of Spicasta Stijena. Here we see two elevations and the road that goes around and to Spicasta Stijena. We see there is no forest. It was cut down during the war. This area was known as "Seven Forests," but during the war people in the city needed firewood, and they came here and cut down trees and took them to Sarajevo to use as firewood. The bit where some forest is left, perhaps 50 metres or 100 metres into the forest, there were lines held by the VRS, and the VRS allowed the trees to be cut. They very rarely fired at people cutting down trees, because they wanted this to become a clearing so they can have a clear view. We were trying to explain to the citizens that it's better not to do that, that they are exposing themselves to danger, but during the war people had used up all the books, all the furniture, all the parquet, and the only thing left was to cut down trees. In this forest, everyone who came to -- came back to Sarajevo after the Dayton Accords, after reintegration began, was able to know how far the VRS lines reached and where exactly they ran.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Based on what you've just said, I have two questions. First of all, how do you know about the people going to the slopes of these hills to cut the trees? And, secondly, how do you know the location, as you've explained it, of the VRS lines?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Of course I know, because I had to do the same thing myself. I went to Sedrenik. I cut down trees and took them to Kosevo, where I lived. So I do know up to what point the lines of the VRS came.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I have these two photographs as Prosecution exhibits, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Only those two or --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then you will download the other picture?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Indeed. I'm advised it's handled best the other way around. We'll up-load these two pictures under a separate 65 ter number, and advise my colleague as soon as that's done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, that will be done. That will be admitted. Exhibit P1980.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And we'll move on now, Mr. Djozo, to the part of your written evidence which is called "Shelling of the area near Markale Market before the Markale II incident of 28 August 1995." In that section, you talk about two separate incidents. The first -- and the first you refer to as a shelling on Dzenetica Cikme Street across the street from Markale Market, in an incident in which children were injured. This is at paragraph 25 of your statement. Do you remember that evidence?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, although you marked a map during your Perisic testimony, setting out the location of those impacts in that incident - and that's 65 ter 13184 - I'd like to use this opportunity so that you can identify those locations for the Trial Chamber perhaps a little bit more clearly. And what I'd actually like on the screen, please, is 65 ter 23001. It's released now. Could you give it another try, please. Thank you. Do you see the image on the screen in front of you, Mr. Djozo?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: I do. I drew this from memory in 2009.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So the date and signature on the bottom, then, is that something you placed there as well?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Does this drawing that you've made relate to the shelling on Dzenetica Cikme Street?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Dzenetica Cikme Street is here in this area below, below the markings where the shell -- shells landed. Above these buildings is Nikola Tesla Street. That's how it was called then. Now it is called Petrarkina Street.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Can I just stop you for a moment. And you indicated, with a hand gesture, Dzenetica Cikme Street. Would you like to write the name of the street on this diagram?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you wait until the Usher assists you, Mr. Djozo. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Indicating in red, then, the name of Dzenetica Cikme Street, or designating Dzenetica Cikme Street, and also Petrarkina Street, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Djozo, between Petrarkina Street and Dzenetica Cikme Street, there are three small star shapes. What do those represent?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Between Dzenetica Cikme Street and Mula Mustafe Baseskije Street, there's the Markale Market. This marking indicates the place where the shell landed, killing many Sarajevans on the market [marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Indicating that with a red circle over one of the asterisk symbols.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, above that, Mr. Djozo, there are three other star-shaped symbols. What do those represent?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: The three little asterisks represent the shell explosions that fell into -- on the Dzenetica Cikme Street that day when the shell dropped. We were informed that on the street of Dzenetica Cikme, there was a shelling, at which time some small children were wounded and killed. I wasn't on duty at the station that day. My colleague was on duty.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And then at the bottom left hand of this drawing, there's another small star-shaped symbol above the words "Markale Trznica." What does that represent?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: That represents the explosion of the shell in front of the Markale II market, an occasion when many inhabitants of Sarajevo were killed as well, and the dates on which this happened are written here.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could this, please, be the next Prosecution exhibit, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I don't think we need to -- the witness needs to sign it again.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I wouldn't think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1981, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And -- thank you. Just for the last exhibit for today, please, could we go back to P1979, which was the marked map.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And while we wait for that: Mr. Djozo, I wonder if you could, looking at this sketch, help us all out by orienting everyone and relating that sketch that you've just referred to to the map you marked earlier. Perhaps he could be assisted and mark this map now with another colour. Could you perhaps circle the area that you represented in the drawing that we've just been discussing?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: I will underline the street Dzenetica Cikme and Petrarkina [marks]. I'm going to indicate with a line where the Mula Mustafe Baseskije Street is [marks]. Between those two streets, Baseskije and Dzenetica Cikme, is where the Markale Market is located.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And that's the area that you sketched out in the drawing that was just admitted as P1981; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And that's marked in green on this map. If we could have that as the next Prosecution exhibit, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1982, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And in terms of relative distances, can you estimate - and I'm only asking for an estimation based on your personal experience on the scene - the distance between the incident on Dzenetica Cikme Street and the Markale II incident in metres?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: It's approximately 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honours, I note the time, and the examination-in-chief would probably continue for another half hour, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Tomorrow morning --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- at 9.00, when we resume. Before we adjourn: Mr. Tieger, when I told Mr. Robinson to co-operate with you as regards the remaining witnesses and their order, I also meant to encourage you to tell us, as well as the Defence, as early as possible if there are any witnesses still on the list whom you are not likely to call, without having to bind yourself thereby.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll rise for today, and we'll resume at 9.00 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 10th day of December, 2010, at 9.00 a.m. 23 24 25
